product.label: Product

hero.title: Build software you can investigate.
hero.subtitle: Connect a result to the recorded steps, inputs and decisions behind it. Give people and coding agents evidence to inspect, with a clear answer when something was not captured.

beats.label: logs
beats.text: Messages tell you something happened. The connections may still be missing.

beats.label: record
beats.text: Capture the steps, tracked values and explicit decisions as the workflow runs.

beats.label: follow the evidence
beats.text: Start at an unexpected result and follow its recorded inputs and choices backward.

beats.label: fix and verify
beats.text: Use the evidence to investigate, then check the repair with a test and a fresh run.

story.closing: Recording does not need an LLM. Enable the evidence you need before the run; missing evidence stays unknown.

idea.lead: Start with the execution and record libraries, add the application capabilities you need, and inspect the captured evidence through a viewer. Different libraries have different records and capture limits.

development.heading: Build with a coding agent. Debug from the record.
development.intro: Use FootPrint in an ordinary application. Your coding agent can inspect its recorded run without putting an AI model inside the application.

steps.title: Build
steps.description: Use named stages, tracked state and explicit decisions.

steps.title: Record
steps.description: Run the application with the required recorders enabled.

steps.title: Inspect
steps.description: Follow the wrong result back through its recorded dependencies.

steps.title: Verify
steps.description: Add a regression test, repair the code and record another run.

development.note: Share the relevant trace slice rather than an entire log dump. The context needed depends on the workflow and tooling; no measured token or speed saving is claimed.

technical.label: Technical

hero.title: Capture connections at runtime.
hero.subtitle: FootPrint executes the workflow and records tracked state and explicit decisions. Foottrace queries supported records. Deterministic readers follow recorded connections; LLM summaries must stay within those findings.

beats.label: configure
beats.text: Enable the required read, write and decision capture before execution.

beats.label: execute
beats.text: The engine records supported activity during traversal, within configured limits.

beats.label: query
beats.text: Follow recorded dependencies backward, or inspect their downstream impact.

beats.label: qualify
beats.text: Name a cause only when the reader has enough evidence. Otherwise return alternatives and gaps.

story.closing: A read-before-write relationship is not proof of semantic derivation. Exact sources, completeness and supported scope determine what a reader can establish.

map.heading: Core patterns and their evidence consumers
map.lawSubline: record during execution; query the evidence afterward
map.evidenceSubline: supported records; explicit readers; disclosed gaps

idea.lead: FootPrint owns execution; Foottrace owns record primitives and readers. Other libraries compose these at their own boundaries. Shared design principles do not imply a shared runtime or interchangeable record formats.

steps.title: Record at traversal time
steps.description: Capture supported activity as it happens, with the required recorders enabled.

steps.title: Preserve causal structure
steps.description: Linear runs, parent-linked trails, and capability graphs retain dependencies, principals, branches, and rejected actions.

steps.title: Compose evidence consumers
steps.description: People and agents inspect the recorded evidence through the view suited to their question.

idea.quote: Recorded dependency is evidence, not proof of real-world cause.

graph.label: Core patterns and their evidence consumers

development.heading: A recorded feedback loop for coding agents
development.intro: The application can run without an LLM. A coding agent consumes a focused record slice during development, using the same public readers and evidence as a human.

steps.title: Model
steps.description: Declare stages, tracked scope and explicit decision helpers.

steps.title: Capture
steps.description: Attach recorders before execution; choose retention and redaction rules.

steps.title: Query
steps.description: Inspect writers, read sources, governing decisions and reported gaps.

steps.title: Check
steps.description: Separate evidence from hypotheses; verify a repair with regression tests and a new run.

development.note: Recording an exact source is opt-in and scope-dependent. Stored evidence, subflows and resumed runs must satisfy the reader’s capture contract; a missing link remains unknown.

business.label: Business

hero.title: See the work behind an answer.
hero.subtitle: When a price, refund or agent answer is questioned, inspect the recorded steps and decisions behind it. See what is supported, what needs investigation and what the system did not capture.

business.solarCaption: Flow, Why and Story — different views over supported execution evidence

beats.label: a question
beats.text: A customer or colleague asks why an outcome happened.

beats.label: the record
beats.text: The workflow has kept the steps, values and decisions it was configured to capture.

beats.label: the evidence
beats.text: Follow the recorded connections instead of piecing together separate messages.

beats.label: the next step
beats.text: Explain the supported finding, investigate a hypothesis or say which evidence is missing.

story.closing: The record supports an investigation. It does not by itself prove correctness, compliance or the cause of an outside event.

development.heading: Help your coding agent investigate your application
development.intro: An application does not need a live AI model to keep a useful record. A developer or coding agent can use that record while building and fixing it.

steps.title: Build
steps.description: Make the important workflow steps explicit.

steps.title: Run
steps.description: Keep the evidence required for the questions you expect.

steps.title: Investigate
steps.description: Follow an unexpected outcome back to the recorded work.

steps.title: Confirm
steps.description: Test the repair and inspect another run before relying on it.

development.note: A focused record can make the investigation easier to follow. Actual time, token use and business savings depend on your application and have not been measured here.

product.title: Follow a recorded application decision
product.description: Inspect tracked reads, writes and explicit decisions behind an outcome, where the required evidence was captured.

technical.title: Execute and record inspectable workflows
technical.description: Named stages, tracked scope and explicit decisions. Opt-in read-source capture links supported reads to their recorded sources; unsupported or incomplete evidence stays unknown.

business.title: Investigate an unexpected outcome
business.description: Inspect what a workflow recorded about a price, refund or routing decision. The record is evidence to investigate, not a guarantee that the result is correct.

product.title: Investigate an agent’s answer
product.description: Inspect the recorded context, model calls, tools and decisions. Test suspected causes rather than treating an explanation as proof.

technical.title: Build agents with inspectable runs
technical.description: An agent runtime with context, tool and model-call evidence. Its cause tools delegate to Foottrace and withhold definite answers when required evidence is incomplete.

business.title: Answer the follow-up from the record
business.description: Review what an agent was shown, which tools ran and what costs were reported. Missing evidence and unknown costs remain visible.

product.title: Investigate a supported saved run
product.description: Query execution records, follow supported dependencies and inspect reported gaps without running an AI model.

technical.title: Read, query and export execution evidence
technical.description: Owns record primitives and readers for replay, time travel, bounded cause/impact queries, exact read-source evidence and optional W3C PROV-O export in JSON-LD.

business.title: Read the record without an AI service
business.description: Inspect retained execution evidence through deterministic tools. A definite finding depends on the record’s completeness and the question being asked.

product.title: One story, several ways to read it
product.description: Turn structured content into an article, a scrolling story or a presentation. FootPrint integration is optional.

technical.title: One content model, multiple presentations
technical.description: Article, scrollytelling and deck views from structured content. The published package declares FootPrint as an optional peer, not an AgentFootprint dependency.

business.title: Present the same material in several formats
business.description: Use one structured source for reading, scrolling and presenting. Choose whether your application needs the optional FootPrint integration.

product.title: Make a film with a making-of record
product.description: Build teaching films from a storyboard and recipe, with a seekable timeline, captions and a recorded production workflow.

technical.title: A film pipeline built on FootPrint
technical.description: StoryReel uses FootPrint and Foottrace directly for its staged production pipeline and making-of record; it does not require AgentFootprint.

business.title: Keep the workflow behind the film
business.description: Create teaching material with a recorded production journey. Inspect the captured making-of steps when a result needs review.

product.title: Compose reusable platform capabilities
product.description: A modular platform framework with focused import paths and shared execution evidence.

technical.title: Modular capabilities over FootPrint
technical.description: The published framework uses FootPrint and Foottrace, keeping reusable platform capabilities behind focused module boundaries.

business.title: Build on shared application capabilities
business.description: Compose the platform pieces your application needs and retain the execution evidence those workflows capture.

product.title: Configure commerce for your shop
product.description: Reusable commerce workflows built on Blueprint, configurable for different shop types.

technical.title: Commerce workflows on Blueprint
technical.description: The published package depends on Blueprint, FootPrint and Foottrace. It adds configurable commerce workflows rather than an agent runtime.

business.title: Reuse the workflow behind your shop
business.description: Configure commerce capabilities for your business. What can be explained later depends on the evidence the application captures and retains.

product.title: Keep the work behind a data result
product.description: Collection and derivation workflows built on FootPrint, with traceable execution evidence.

technical.title: Collection and derivation over FootPrint
technical.description: The published package uses FootPrint and Foottrace directly. Captured execution evidence helps investigate a data result; it does not prove a source is correct.

business.title: Review how a result was produced
business.description: Follow recorded collection and derivation steps when a number is questioned. Missing source evidence remains unknown.

product.title: Make applications agent-operable
product.description: Give agents a typed map of the app's real capabilities while preserving permissions, confirmation gates, and the signed-in user's control.

technical.title: Typed capability and action graph
technical.description: Exposes live application capabilities as a typed skill graph over MCP, with preconditions, permissions, guide mode, action boundaries, and confirmation gates.

business.title: Let agents operate your app — inside the gates you already have
business.description: Agents use the application’s declared capabilities, permissions and confirmation gates. People retain control of actions that require approval; the application records the evidence those boundaries capture.

product.title: Preserve recorded exploration paths
product.description: Keep supported human and agent branches of an analysis, compare paths and replay retained findings. Recording settings and declared statistical obligations still matter.

technical.title: Branchable exploration provenance
technical.description: Append-only parent-linked commits, mixed-principal causes, named branches, comparison, replay and adoption, declared analyses, and a shared online-FDR ledger.

business.title: Show how a number was arrived at
business.description: Review retained paths through an analysis, including recorded alternatives, so a figure can be inspected alongside the work behind it. Unrecorded source activity remains unknown.

product.title: Flow Lens · inspect a recorded run
product.description: Explore recorded steps, state and supported variable traces. Choose a recorded subflow invocation where the record format supports it.

technical.title: Flow Lens · inspect execution evidence
technical.description: React views for flowcharts, state, replay and variable tracing over supported FootPrint records. Missing or unsupported evidence is shown explicitly.

business.title: Flow Lens · follow the recorded work
business.description: Walk the captured steps and values behind a workflow result. The viewer shows the evidence available; it cannot recover data that was not recorded.

product.title: Why Lens · inspect context and tools
product.description: Compare recorded messages, prompts, tool activity, decisions and cost while investigating an agent run.

technical.title: Why Lens · inspect the agent timeline
technical.description: A React debugger for supported AgentFootprint records, aligning messages, prompts, tool calls, decision scope and reported cost.

business.title: Why Lens · inspect the evidence behind an answer
business.description: Read the recorded context and tool activity together. A suspected cause still needs to be tested; the viewer does not turn a hypothesis into proof.

product.title: Story Lens · follow the recorded journey
product.description: Present a supported agent record as a story a person can replay and inspect. The story explains captured evidence, not a model’s hidden reasoning.

technical.title: Story Lens · replay supported agent evidence
technical.description: A scrubbable replay of supported AgentFootprint records, exposing captured roles, tools and recorded alternatives.

business.title: Story Lens · explain the recorded work
business.description: Give a colleague or reviewer a readable journey through the evidence that was captured, with room to question the interpretation.
